Expected Behavior: render_scene_with_repair renders, and while status in {render-error, render-timeout} with an API key, feeds an 8000-char stderr tail (12000 at the repair prompt) plus — for timeouts — actionable load-reduction direction to SceneGenerator.repair (temp 0.2), compile+safety+lint-checks the fix, and re-renders (max_repairs=2). User Story: As a user, a reply cut off at the token limit fails cleanly instead of yielding broken code.

User Story: As a user, generated scene code can't execute arbitrary host actions from the render subprocess.

User Story: As a user, the pipeline stops repeating the same render mistakes across runs.

User Story: As a user without a key (or after LLM failure), the fallback video still shows MY physics domain.

User Story: As a user, my scene is first *directed* (creative treatment), then *implemented* — not improvised in one shot.
Expected Behavior: SceneGenerator.storyboard() runs a hot directing pass (temp 0.9) returning strict JSON (concept/staging/palette/3 acts with durations/hero_frame/idle_loop/narration script); _generate_remote then implements the locked storyboard cold (temp 0.15) via SCENE_CODEGEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT. Any storyboard failure fails soft to the proven single-call cinematic path (temp 0.4). The storyboard rides on SceneBundle.storyboard through the cache.
Notes: Verified: hot storyboard@0.9 → cold codegen@0.15; fail-soft (F107)

Feature: Perceptual critique loop (VLM watches the video)
User Story: As a user with a vision model configured, rendered videos are actually *watched* and revised until they pass a quality rubric.
Expected Behavior: scene_critic samples frames uniformly (PyAV — Manim's own backend — with ffmpeg-CLI fallback), sends them + the storyboard/brief to settings.vision_model (AETHERLAB_VISION_MODEL / app-config), and returns ship/revise + score + issues against a 5-point rubric (legibility/composition/palette/structure/substance). render_scene_with_repair loops SceneGenerator.revise() (aesthetic rewrite, distinct from crash repair) up to max_revisions=2; a revision is adopted only if it still renders (never downgrades a shipped cut). No vision model → verdict 'skipped', pipeline unchanged.
Notes: Verified: critique loop wired + fail-soft; sampled 3 frames via PyAV (F108)

User Story: As a user, zooming keeps the data point under my cursor pinned under the cursor, with a smooth glide instead of jumps.
Expected Behavior: wheelEvent retargets a 120ms OutCubic QVariantAnimation toward the new zoom; every animation frame re-applies _apply_zoom(zoom, anchor_px), which measures the anchor's data coords before/after the zoom and shifts _pan_offset by the delta, so the anchored point is invariant. Ctrl+0 and double-click reset.
Notes: Verified: zoom anchors cursor; 120ms smooth-zoom animation wired

User Story: As a user, the comet trail stays glued to the curve through zoom/pan, and the sweep speed never depends on frame rate.
Expected Behavior: Trail points are stored as (x, y) DATA coords and mapped to pixels at paint time (<=24 points). The tracer advances by QElapsedTimer wall-clock dt (clamped 0.25s after stalls) so one sweep takes SWEEP_SECONDS=6.0 exactly; the first tick after pause/resume only restarts the clock.
Notes: Verified: data-space trail survives zoom/pan; wall-clock sweep (6s), no resume jump

User Story: As a user, hovering near a curve snaps the crosshair to the nearest sample and shows me (t, x, y), not just raw cursor coordinates.
Expected Behavior: Paint publishes per-curve pixel arrays; _update_hover does a vectorized nanargmin over visible non-reference curves and snaps within 24px — crosshair locks to the sample, a ring marks it, the readout shows t plus data coords, and the legend entry highlights. Beyond 24px it falls back to raw coords.
Notes: Verified: snaps within 24px with (t,x,y); raw-coords fallback beyond

User Story: As a maintainer, every canvas color comes from one palette that mirrors the design tokens.
Expected Behavior: Module-level CANVAS_PALETTE dict (documented as mirroring ui/style.py) consumed by every draw call, curve factory, and role assignment; the module body contains zero stray hex literals (asserted by test F112).

User Story: As a user, zooming is instant (no recompute) and asymptotes render as separate arms instead of a false bridge.
Expected Behavior: Curve samples (t, xs, ys) are cached keyed by (params, t_range, t_steps) only — zoom/pan never rebuilds them; the data-to-pixel affine map is re-applied per paint with vectorized numpy into QPolygonF via the sip buffer (no per-point Python loops). Non-finite samples split polylines into finite runs (>=2 points), so 1/t draws exactly 2 branches.
Notes: Verified: viewport-independent sample cache; 1/t = 2 branches, no bridge

The solver prompt documents the schema with an example; fallback_plot_payload showcases oscillation + two dashed envelopes.

A 2px t-progress bar hugs the bottom axis (brighter while scrubbing). Double-click calls reset_view() alongside Ctrl+0.

User Story: As a student, I install AetherLab with one Setup.exe and scenes render even without LaTeX installed.
